title: The training principles series: aesthetics
summary: NH defines 'aesthetics' in bodybuilding as the Apollonian physique (wide shoulders, narrow hips, V-taper, low bodyfat) and explains why his own frame (wide waist, short clavicles) can't achieve it. He offers the Herculean physique as an alternative he aspires to, rejects somatotypes, and argues any aesthetic is valid if you like what you see.

claims.claim: In bodybuilding, 'aesthetics' refers to the Apollonian physique: narrow hips, wide shoulders, a strong V-taper, low bodyfat and smaller legs.
Size has been taking over bodybuilding, even in categories meant to be aesthetic, which now reward massive legs and arms.
YouTube 'aesthetic' figures are typically over six feet tall, very lean, with Apollonian proportions.
NH can't achieve the Apollonian look: his waist is much wider than his narrow hips, and his short clavicles give him narrow shoulders and a stocky look.
The Herculean physique is the alternative: stockier, thicker waist, bigger abs and especially bigger limbs; NH aspires to it as cooler and suited to his frame.
For his frame, getting very lean would look odd since his waist won't trim to match his hips, so he will always stay at a higher bodyfat.
Assess yourself objectively to judge whether you can pull off the Apollonian look before pursuing it.
Somatotypes (ectomorph, mesomorph) don't exist as fixed categories; you can evolve in any direction, helped or hindered by your natural frame.
Any aesthetic is valid; don't be ashamed to pursue a different look or to accept that some looks are out of reach and focus on what makes you look better.
Your bodybuilding goals are your own: if you want big legs or big arms, build them.
Bodybuilding is crafting a vessel your spirit enjoys inhabiting; what matters is whether you like what you see in the mirror.
